import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 1.74 (Tarski monster topologizability)

by V. P. Platonov

Problem 1.74 asks to describe all "minimal topological groups" in Platonov's
sense: non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups all of whose proper closed
subgroups are discrete. A natural test case: does there exist a Tarski monster
group admitting a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology? A Tarski monster
would be a minimal group in this sense, since all its proper subgroups are
finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.74»

/--
A Tarski monster group: an infinite group in which every non-trivial proper
subgroup has order a fixed prime $p$.
-/
def IsTarskiMonster (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Infinite G ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊥ → H ≠ ⊤ → Nat.card H = p

/--
Does there exist a Tarski monster group that admits a non-discrete Hausdorff
group topology?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G),
      IsTarskiMonster G ∧ IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧
      ¬ DiscreteTopology G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.74»

findings.description: The declaration replaces Problem 1.74's classification task with a yes/no existence question: whether some Tarski monster admits a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology. Being such a topologized Tarski monster is sufficient for Platonov-minimality, but is not an equivalent characterization, and existence does not classify the requested groups. For example, the usual additive real line is Platonov-minimal—all proper closed subgroups are discrete—but is not a Tarski monster. Both facts were verified in Lean. The docstring's explicitly designated 'natural test case' therefore does not formalize the source problem, and no declaration in the file states the classification task.
findings.source_evidence: The Kourovka Notebook, arXiv:1401.0300v40, Problem 1.74 (LaTeX source 21tkt.tex, lines 432–436): 'Describe all minimal topological groups, that is, non-discrete groups all of whose closed subgroups are discrete. The minimal locally compact groups can be described without much effort. At the same time, the problem is probably complicated in the general case.' The same text remains in https://arxiv.org/html/1401.0300v46#p66. Neither version poses the Tarski-monster existence question.
findings.suggested_fix: Formalize an answer-valued classification of Platonov-minimal topological groups. The defining property should include IsTopologicalGroup G, T2Space G, ¬ DiscreteTopology G, and ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H. The answer must describe all groups/topologies satisfying this property, rather than merely assert existence in the Tarski subclass. The current existential can be retained as a separately identified, solved related result with its own primary citation.

status_issues.source_status: The Tarski-monster existence question actually formalized here was answered affirmatively by A. A. Klyachko, A. Yu. Olshanskii, and D. V. Osin in 2013. Their Theorem 1.4 constructs a topologizable Tarski monster of every sufficiently large odd exponent n. Choosing n to be a sufficiently large prime p gives the exact prime-order subgroup condition in this file: each nontrivial proper subgroup is finite cyclic, and its order divides p, so its order is p. This does not solve Platonov's full classification problem.
status_issues.evidence: Klyachko–Olshanskii–Osin, On topologizable and non-topologizable groups, Topology and its Applications 160 (2013), 2104–2120, Theorem 1.4: 'For every sufficiently large odd n ∈ ℕ there exists a topologizable Tarski Monster of exponent n.' The introduction defines topologizable as admitting a non-discrete Hausdorff group topology. https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7895 ; https://arxiv.org/e-print/1210.7895v3
status_issues.suggested_change: If this existential is retained, mark it category research solved, replace answer(sorry) by answer(True), and cite Theorem 1.4. Do not mark the original classification problem solved.

reformulations.difference: The definition uses Nat.card H = p without separately asserting that each nontrivial proper subgroup is finite and cyclic, as in the standard prime-order Tarski-monster definition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since p is prime, p ≠ 0. Thus Nat.card H = p forces H to be finite: Nat.card of an infinite type is zero. Every group of prime order is cyclic. Conversely, a finite cyclic subgroup of order p satisfies Nat.card H = p. The exact equivalence with a version explicitly requiring Finite H ∧ IsCyclic H ∧ Nat.card H = p was proved as tarski_explicit_finite_cyclic in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Problem 1.74 (Minimal topological groups)

by V. P. Platonov

Problem 1.74 asks to describe all "minimal topological groups" in Platonov's
sense: non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups all of whose proper closed
subgroups are discrete. A Tarski monster equipped with a non-discrete Hausdorff
group topology is minimal in this sense, since all its proper subgroups are
finite (hence discrete in any Hausdorff group topology).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«1.74»

/--
A Tarski monster group: an infinite group in which every non-trivial proper
subgroup has order a fixed prime $p$.
-/
def IsTarskiMonster (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Infinite G ∧ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧
    ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊥ → H ≠ ⊤ → Nat.card H = p

/--
Describe all non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups whose proper closed
subgroups are discrete. The answer is a predicate on a type equipped with a
group structure and a topology.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka_1_74 :
    (fun (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : TopologicalSpace G) =>
      IsTopologicalGroup G ∧ T2Space G ∧ ¬ DiscreteTopology G ∧
        ∀ H : Subgroup G, H ≠ ⊤ → IsClosed (H : Set G) → DiscreteTopology H) =
      answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«1.74»
